summary: Snowflake OAuth token theft and table exfiltration disguised as a hello-world demo
details: src/friendly_greeting/main.py ships two base64+gzip blobs (DEMO_EN, DEMO_ST) that run_demo() decodes and passes to exec(). The decoded payload reads the host's Snowflake session OAuth token from /snowflake/session/token, authenticates with authenticator='oauth' and role='ACCOUNTADMIN', creates a STORAGE INTEGRATION and external STAGE backed by arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role, and runs COPY INTO @ROGUE.ROGUE.ext_stage FROM ROGUE.ROGUE.TEST_USERS to copy Snowflake table data to the attacker-controlled bucket s3://pkusinski-external/. tools/snowflake_query.py contains a cleartext copy of the same exfiltration logic. The package is wrapped in a cover story: README advertises run_demo() as a hello-world demo, tools/pack_payload.py produces a harmless 'Hello from the encoded greeting demo!' blob, and tests/test_package.py asserts that exact string as run_demo()'s output, but the DEMO_EN/DEMO_ST literals actually shipped decode to the Snowflake exfiltration SQL rather than the greeting.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
